title: Git - Clicking "Stage Changes" after resolving a merge conflict with "Accept All Current" results in no empty commit merge being staged
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes



- VS Code Version: 1.58.2 or today's Insiders
OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.19043

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Create a git branch with a change, e.g. version change in package.json.
2. Create another git branch with a conflicting change, e.g. a different version.
3. From the Source Control view, use the Merge Branch... option to merge one branch into the other.
4. When the conflict occurs, right-click on the conflicting file and choose "Accept All Current".
5. Save the changed file.
6. Click the "Stage Changes" button:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/19859882/127209511-28a2c6a4-4f1b-4591-805a-3160d7aa906c.png)

Bug: No changes are staged and there is no other UI indication of how to conclude the merge (the fix would be to add some UI indication). Use the steps below to try to workaround the issue:

7. Create some new files that are unstaged and not added to git. (in a normal scenario, these files would already exist, and they're just created in this step in order to repro the issue).
8. Use the Commit command in the UI.

Bug 2: A popup appears that doesn't give any option to commit the empty change and instead it asks about staging the new files. Either the 1st bug could be fixed or it should give another option to Create Empty Commit.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/19859882/127210213-eaa4b7ab-06f0-4157-b5e0-bd4a76687adc.png)

The workaround is to delete all the unstaged files, which and then use the Commit command, which brings up a "Create Empty Commit" popup, which causes the merge to be completed.

title: Editor: scroll jumps randomly (related to Chrome, Electron, xinput)
body:
- VSCode Version: starting at 1.13.0, up to current
- OS Version: Fedora 24-27

Looks like VS Code is listening to mouse scroll events, even while it is not active in the window.
Related: 
https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=608246
https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=807187


**Steps to Reproduce**
requirements: Browser (Chromium / Firefox / Google Chrome), VSCode Editor (Any file type. Ideally a long file to ensure the scroll is visible.)

VSCode: Leave cursor at top of file.
Browser: Scroll, excessively, (For a few seconds) down the page. Even if it's a blank tab with no content.
VSCode: Scroll, ever so slightly, in any direction.
You'll find the editor will jump suddenly further down the active file.

It seems VSCode is receiving the scroll events, for whatever reason; which are all suddenly evaluated upon any form of scroll input in the editor.

**Updates based on comments**

GUESS: Appears to be an issue with Electron and some input libraries?
Is not isolated to VScode
Fix: Does not yet exist.

Linux Workarounds (Not to be confused with a fix)

imwheel - not suitable for all users
wayland - not suitable for all users
Note: Ubuntu 19.04 (Desktop) appears to be using Wayland.

I'm not sure we will see further updates in here, which is a bit disappointing from the developers, given the amount of comments from affected people. I would like to have some official guidance, even if it's pointing us to other resources.

title: Proposal: Add option to automatically start task runners' tasks
body:
In #1789 I suggested to add a [INLINE_CODE] pragma comment to precede task runner tasks so the IDE will be able to recognize task runner tasks. This proposal here augments the mentioned proposal.
Whenever a project is opened in VS Code, which is indicated by the following preconditions: - a folder gets opened which contains one or more [INLINE_CODE] files - any of those [INLINE_CODE] files contains one or more [INLINE_CODE] pragma comments - any of those [INLINE_CODE] pragma comments comes with an [INLINE_CODE] property set ... then the tasks marked with [INLINE_CODE] should automatically be executed. Here's a screenshot depicting how the [INLINE_CODE] property is suggested to be applied: ![auto run 1](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/9283914/12098517/2161e340-b323-11e5-854d-c4357cef5c60.png)
Depending on user/workspace settings, a confirmation dialog might be displayed before the tasks are automatically getting started: ![auto run 2](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/9283914/12098540/3f001566-b323-11e5-8381-5af2a884aacc.png)
Browsing for the [INLINE_CODE] pragma comment in all [INLINE_CODE] files within the current project root folder might become time consuming, given that there may be many large [INLINE_CODE] files in the project folder. So browsing should be performed asynchronously.
#### The following behaviour is suggested: 1. Browsing [INLINE_CODE] files in the current project root folder for containing [INLINE_CODE] should be performed asynchronously after the folder has been opened in Code. 2. A user/workspace setting should be introduced to control whether the confirmation dialog box should be displayed and whether automatic execution of tasks should be performed anyway. The setting should come with the following enumeration: - [INLINE_CODE] // always run autostart tasks without showing the confirmation dialog box - [INLINE_CODE] // as soon as the first [INLINE_CODE] pragma comment is parsed by the browser a
